Authored changes are limited to src/ptest/scheduler.py, tests/ng/test_scheduler.py and this report. The pre-existing untracked .pipeline/out/task-4-luna-response.json was preserved. Bootstrap and graphify generated only their local ignored artifacts.

Final required test command: scripts/ptest-bootstrap tests/ng/test_scheduler.py --durations=10. Exit 0; exact summary: 91 passed, 2 warnings in 1.00s. Slowest recorded test call: 0.03s, below the 0.5s requirement. No full suite or raw test runner was invoked. git diff --check: exit 0, empty output. graphify update .: exit 0, local AST-only update, 3188 nodes, 5906 edges, 232 communities.

Observed TDD evidence: initial 31-case run failed 19/passed 12 (its verbose output was tool-truncated; only those observed totals are claimed). Expanded pre-implementation RED: 26 failed, 26 passed in 0.56s. First implementation: 51 passed/1 failed; the remaining failure was duplicate lock event instrumentation, corrected to emit once. CPU RED: 3 failed, 63 passed in 0.68s; subsequent GREEN: 66 passed, 2 warnings in 0.67s. Release-race RED: 2 failed, 71 passed, 2 warnings in 0.91s; subsequent GREEN: 73 passed, 2 warnings in 0.83s. Fixture-boundary RED: 2 failed, 84 passed, 2 warnings in 1.00s; subsequent GREEN: 86 passed, 2 warnings in 0.86s. Transaction/deadline RED: 3 failed, 86 deselected in 0.18s; subsequent GREEN: 89 passed, 2 warnings in 0.89s. Two additional presentation/memory-lowering cases passed in the final 91-case run. Tests already green on introduction are regression coverage, not claimed RED evidence.

Finding 1: _recovery_view preserves nonce/generation-bound FINALIZING when the recorded owner remains live after guard/group absence; finish independently authenticates the grant and transitions FINALIZING before release. Evidence: test_poller_preserves_live_finalizer_and_checkout_charge; test_real_guard_forged_proof_and_multiprocess_finalizer_poller[False] uses a real session leader, orderly reaping, a separate polling process and bounded event sequence ending FINALIZING -> RELEASED.

Finding 2: _recover_boot_locked reads boot/config after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, cancels previous unfinished rows with ownership-uncertain and incomplete outcomes, invalidates grants, rebases monotonic fields, clears only old-boot observations and advances the domain generation without replacing the ledger. Read-only reconcile computes the same projection without writes. Evidence: test_new_boot_atomically_cancels_old_work_and_rebases_time; test_unavailable_boot_never_mutates_existing_state. Boot transition is simulated, not an actual host reboot.

Findings 3 and 5: None process identity is indeterminate; only an independent ESRCH establishes absence. finish rejects forged/stale/future/pre-grant proofs, fresh-probes the group, rechecks recorded descendants after that probe and requires current matching owner plus proven guard absence. Evidence: caller_quiescence_booleans_cannot_release_live_or_unknown_group; unregistered_grant_releases_only_for_proven_absence[none,eperm,reuse,uid,absent]; proof_before_grant_or_from_future_cannot_release; stale_platform_group_observation_cannot_authorize_release; dead_or_uncertain_owner_never_promotes_pass; real live fixture group forged-proof rejection.

Findings 4 and 6: fast deterministic barriers, pipes, bounded transition logs and fake monotonic clocks cover concurrent first use, slot/job/memory/lock admission, FIFO checkout/resource/exclusive contention, default 480-second queue survival, explicit deadlines behind a blocked head and pending-cap reclamation. Deadline checks now sample time after acquiring the write transaction. Evidence: multiprocess_admission_event_log_respects_bounds[slots,jobs,memory,lock]; atomic_admission_honors_each_independent_resource_bound; default_queue_survives_two_240_second_predecessors; deadline_behind_blocked_head_expires_and_frees_pending_capacity; enqueue_expires_all_deadlines_before_pending_limit_check; deadline_is_rechecked_after_waiting_for_the_transaction. Tests contain no arbitrary sleep synchronization.

Finding 7: all partial-state decisions occur under the bootstrap lock, and the validated ledger connection is reused. Marker inode/device is bound in the fresh private schema. Only a valid, identity-bound initialized schema with zero jobs/resources/observations and an unfinished marker publication can be completed; unidentified empty or previously used ledgers are not recreated. Evidence: two_initializers_serialize_partial_marker_publication; interrupted_empty_initialization_completes_marker_without_recreating; unidentified_empty_ledger_is_never_initialized_over; hostile_or_partial_existing_state_never_recreates_ledger; hostile_domain_marker_is_rejected_without_outside_writes; database_replacement_between_validation_and_open_is_rejected; storage_failure_does_not_admit_or_fall_back. Additional injected SQLite write/commit failures prove typed errors, rollback and unconditional connection closure.

Finding 8: reconcile uses a read-only connection/transaction and pure ownership/recovery projections. Existing ledger bytes, mtimes and directory entries are unchanged during inspection. Current queued wait is reported. Additive effective_limits(domain) returns the already-frozen EffectiveLimits record for absent, configured-memory and default-no-budget cases without creating state; repo_workers remains null because no repository config is supplied. All five frozen scheduler function signatures remain unchanged. Evidence: existing_status_is_read_only_and_reports_current_queue_wait; reconcile_on_an_absent_normal_domain_is_non_mutating; effective_limits_are_typed_read_only_and_reflect_deferred_increase[None,64].

Findings 9 and 10: bounded live ancestry rejects active same-domain nesting; inaccessible ancestry fails ownership-uncertain without reading inherited environment. The design's private observations table retains observed descendant identities and sticky uncertainty; both live/unknown escaped descendants and a child escaping during the final absence probe prevent release. Evidence: nested_active_guard_and_inaccessible_ancestry_fail_closed; observed_escape_survives_reparenting_and_blocks_forged_release; unknown_descendant_scan_is_persisted_even_after_guard_exits; reported_unknown_escape_is_not_forgotten_by_a_later_proof; descendant_escaping_during_absence_probe_retains_charge. Escaped/unknown observations are deterministic simulated kernel facts; real daemon-containment is not claimed.

Finding 11: decreases and introducing a memory budget apply while preserving existing charges; any loosening/removal waits for no active or pending rows, then advances config generation. Existing unknown reservations consume a newly introduced budget conservatively. Persisted defaults include affinity, logical CPU count and supported Linux cgroup-v2 ancestor quota/cpuset minima; unavailable layout yields one CPU with a warning. Shared schema/protocol/queue/pending/terminal constants are imported from contracts. Evidence: memory_budget_loosening_waits_for_idle[128,None]; lowering_limits_and_introducing_memory_budget_keep_existing_charge; lowered_memory_budget_waits_for_existing_reservation_to_drain; persisted_defaults_include_cgroup_ancestor_bounds; unreadable_cpu_quota_falls_back_to_one_with_diagnostic.

Finding 12: finish authenticates all Grant fields before allowing a proof failure to affect the row. Evidence: forged_grant_never_poisons_a_legitimate_row[nonce,generation,domain_id,slots,memory_estimate_mb,reserved_memory_mb] compares ledger bytes before/after rejection; matching insufficient proofs retain charge as UNCERTAIN.

Secure-by-spec negative contracts: Identity—missing/raced/reused/split observations cannot free a live charge. Authorization—full nonce/generation/domain/resource grant matching gates finalization. Tenancy—account-canonical and explicit fixture domains/checkout confinement are retained. Input—malformed, oversized, replaced, linked, wrong-mode and partial private state fails closed. State—bootstrap/poll/finalize/boot races cannot duplicate grants; failed writes roll back. Exposure—safe typed errors avoid raw SQLite errors; runtime does not read environment/config redirects, legacy config, command lines or process environments. Availability—pending/terminal/descendant/ancestry/kernel-read bounds, FIFO and deadline reclamation remain finite. Dependencies—only existing local stdlib/psutil/files/storage/contracts are used; no new package or remote dependency. Extra abuse cases discovered during implementation: stale group-observation timestamps, post-probe descendant escape, bool fixture version, oversized miniature fixture budget, pre-lock deadline sampling and connection leakage after commit failure.

Scoped audit-spec self-review: VERDICT APPROVE for this scoped repair (the identified transaction/deadline and fixture-boundary findings were repaired and verified before this report). Final scoped findings: no unresolved blocking finding from the twelve-item repair brief. Coverage: correctness/state races, architecture/public records, local process/filesystem trust boundaries, atomic data changes, deterministic tests, bounded observations, duplicate timeout/version/default cleanup and no remote/legacy/launcher dependency. This is the repair owner's self-review, not the controller's independent Opus re-review. Full release/platform/security verification remains outside this task.
